extracted.intended_audience: readers looking up episode information (fans, researchers, TV editors), people cataloguing The Daily Show episodes
extracted.subtask_description: A structured episode guide for a satirical news program (The Daily Show) that records episode number, date, host, guests, promoted works, and short synopses of segments and topics covered. Useful for cataloguing, reference, or research into episode content and recurring segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode metadata fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Each episode entry lists: 'No. overall', 'No. in season', 'Date', 'Hosted by', 'Guest(s)', 'Promotion'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these fields consistently to identify and sort episodes; include exact date, host name, guest(s), and any promoted works (books, films, podcasts). Examples from the page: 'No. overall', 'No. in season', 'Date', 'Hosted by', 'Guest(s)', 'Promotion'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live episode indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Episodes sometimes marked as 'Live episode' or 'live episode from [location]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag episodes that were broadcast live or from special locations (e.g., conventions, cities) as this often correlates with immediate debate/coverage content and different production needs. Examples: 'Live episode', 'live episode from Chicago', 'Live episode Jon Stewart'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode structure (host analysis + correspondents + guest interview + closing bit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical structure: host opens with analysis/monologue (Jon/other hosts analyze events), correspondents present field pieces or recurring segments, followed by a guest interview, then a closing recurring gag/segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synopses should capture this sequence: what the host analyzed, which correspondent pieces aired, the guest's central topic/promotion, and the closing bit. Examples across entries: host analyzing debates or events, correspondent Troy Iwata reports, guest discusses their book/film, 'Your Moment of Zen' closes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion / guest tie-in
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Promotion' field lists books, films, podcasts, or other works guests are promoting (e.g., 'The Bear', 'Cost Plus Drugs', 'Maybe You Should Talk to Someone').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the promoted work's title and medium; use these to contextualize interview topics. Many guest synopsis lines explicitly link discussion to their promoted work (author discusses the book; actor discusses a film/show).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: 'Headlines'
rubrics_metrics.description: A short segment that covers current headlines and satirizes topical news (politics, celebrity, oddities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries append topics covered in 'Headlines' (e.g., guilty verdict against Hunter Biden; Target limiting LGBT merchandise). Use 'Headlines' to summarize quick-hit jokes or bits about several news items in a single bullet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: 'InDecision 2024'
rubrics_metrics.description: Election-cycle coverage and satire branded as 'InDecision 2024' focusing on campaign events, debates, rallies, and political gaffes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this label for sustained election-related analysis or recurring election-themed jokes (e.g., coverage of debates, Trump/Harris events, RNC/DNC nights). The page lists many 'InDecision 2024' examples tied to debates and campaign news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: 'Your Moment of Zen'
rubrics_metrics.description: A short closing gag or ironic clip labeled 'Your Moment of Zen' often highlighting a ridiculous political/media moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the quoted clip or the punchline as the synopsis shows (examples: Fox & Friends dismisses Macron's language, Trump's 'I have concepts of a plan').

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: 'In My Opinion'
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest-opinion-style short pieces where commentators articulate direct views (often labeled 'In My Opinion').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the commentator and the central opinion or argument (e.g., Charlamagne tha God arguing Democrats should be more direct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: 'Back in Black'
rubrics_metrics.description: Lewis Black's rant segment providing angry, comedic critique on topical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture the target and tone of the rant (e.g., Lewis Black on fire departments or corporate America expanding into summer camps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: 'Sports War'
rubrics_metrics.description: A sports-focused debate/comedy bit (e.g., Ronny and Jordan arguing/wagering over sports incidents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the sports topics debated and any wagers or punchlines; used to inject sports-related comedic banter into episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: 'Jordan Klepper Fingers the Pulse' (field reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: On-the-ground correspondent reporting capturing the views and performative behaviors of political supporters/attendees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the venue and the performative claims observed (e.g., Klepper at a Trump rally in Racine, WI) and how the segment frames supporter rhetoric or actions for satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring sketch/team bit: 'The Best F#@king News Team'
rubrics_metrics.description: A recurring sketch where cast members enact a fictional news team offering absurd takes on events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the sketch's satirical premise and which cast members perform; used as a comedic device to parody news presentation and corporate culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring feature: 'The Daily Showography'
rubrics_metrics.description: A quick profile/history-style bit highlighting a person's career or a topical figure with comedic framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to provide context about a public figure or trend with a humorous slant (e.g., 'The Daily Showography' of Jeff Bezos).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of satire to critique politics and media
rubrics_metrics.description: Across entries, the show uses humor to debunk claims, call out hypocrisy, and critique media and political narratives (e.g., debunking crime-rate obsessions, calling out media for allowing vagaries to fester).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episode summaries should capture both the comedic angle and the critical target; examples show host Jon Stewart 'calls out' conservatives and media, and correspondents expose absurdities. This is a stylistic/content criterion for the show's output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cast/correspondent role labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Episode notes identify which correspondent (e.g., Ronny Chieng, Jordan Klepper, Michael Kosta, Desi Lydic, Troy Iwata) performs specific field pieces, recurring segments, or sports bits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute field pieces and recurring bits to the correct correspondent, since the cast member frames perspective and style (e.g., Ronny covers NBA/Celtics material; Troy Iwata reports oddities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special event coverage (conventions, debates, rallies)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the show covers conventions, debates, or rallies, entries note special framing ('InDecision 2024: The First Presidential Debate', 'The Republican National Convention — Donald Trump Fists America').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark episodes tied to live political events with clear event labels and summarize the show's critical angle; such episodes often replace normal structure with event-driven analysis and field pieces.
